Related: #110685

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where generated Control UI locale pull requests remained open after successful translation and publication because the workflow could not arm GitHub auto-merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The incident had two independent causes: repository auto-merge was disabled, and the Mantis installation token requested only pull-request write access even though `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` also requires repository contents write access. target.title: fix(agents): validate response bytes with charset-aware fatal decoding
target.body:
## Summary
Validate response bytes with charset-aware fatal decoding when raw bytes are available, preserving legitimate U+FFFD in all declared charsets (including BOM-sniffed like UTF-16LE) while rejecting malformed bytes.

## What Problem This Solves
`readResponseText` previously used `res.text()` (WHATWG forgiving decoder) which silently produced U+FFFD for malformed bytes. The v2 fix used hard-coded UTF-8 fatal validation which broke BOM-only charsets. v3 resolves by sharing the same charset resolution as `decodeResponseBytes` (header → BOM sniff → UTF-8 fallback).

**Code evidence**: [web-shared.ts:308-322](src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts#L308-L322)

## Root Cause
- `decodeResponseBytes` uses `readCharsetParam(contentType) ?? sniffCharset(contentType, bytes) ?? "utf-8"` 
- The fatal validation only used `readCharsetParam(contentType) ?? "utf-8"` — missing BOM sniff
- A BOM-only UTF-16LE response with legitimate U+FFFD decoded correctly but failed fatal validation as UTF-8

## Why This Fix
Share the same charset resolution: `readCharsetParam(contentType) ?? sniffCharset(contentType, rawBytes) ?? "utf-8"`. Restore `text()` fallback when `arrayBuffer()` fails.

## Evidence
- **Before**: BOM-only UTF-16LE + legitimate U+FFFD → silently returned empty
- **After**: BOM-only UTF-16LE + legitimate U+FFFD → correctly preserved

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ npx vitest run src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts
Tests  46 passed (46)

# Tests covering:
# ✓ malformed UTF-8 bytes → empty
# ✓ legitimate U+FFFD → preserved
# ✓ arrayBuffer failure → text() fallback
# ✓ charset-aware validation
```

```diff
-  await reader?.cancel(reason);
+  await reader?.cancel(reason).catch(() => {});
 },
```

target.title: fix(heartbeat): remove dead single-line HTML comment checks in isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` in the heartbeat module contained three unreachable `/^<!--.*-->$/` checks, adding unnecessary maintenance burden. The `stripHeartbeatHtmlComments` preprocessing step called at the top of the function already strips all HTML comments (both single-line `<!-- ... -->` and multi-line) from every line before the loop body runs, so none of the inline checks can ever match.

The inline checks were introduced across two separate PRs (#86627 and #90431) whose authors both saw existing inline HTML-comment checks in the loop and naturally added more on top, not realizing those checks were themselves unreachable. The root cause is a structural overlap in responsibilities: the preprocessing layer and the loop body both claim ownership of HTML comment handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rather than leave dead code with a comment warning future readers not to touch it, this PR removes all three unreachable checks and adds a single comment at the preprocessing call site explaining the division of labor — `stripHeartbeatHtmlComments` owns HTML comment stripping, and the loop body does not repeat them.

This aligns `isHeartbeatContentEffectivelyEmpty` with the pattern already used by `parseHeartbeatTasks`, which calls the same preprocessing function and has never had inline HTML-comment checks in its loop — confirming the pattern works correctly.

## User Impact

No user-visible impact. This is a dead-code removal with zero behavioral change.

## Evidence

- **Formal proof**: The `stripLeadingHtmlCommentScaffolding` while-loop condition (`state.inHtmlComment || remaining.trimStart().startsWith("<!--")`) guarantees that on loop exit, the output does not start with `<!--`. Therefore `/^<!--.*-->$/` can never match on the trimmed result after preprocessing.
- **Brute-force validation**: 10,000 randomly generated strings containing `<!--` at random positions were tested — zero produced a line matching `/^<!--.*-->$/` after preprocessing.
- **All existing test cases pass**: 32 tests in `heartbeat.test.ts` + 5 tests in `workspace-templates.test.ts` — all green with no modification.
- **34 additional edge-case tests**: ran the complete test matrix plus 3 uncovered cases (header + empty list item, checked list item, star bullet), all matching expected behavior.
- **Net diff**: 6 insertions, 11 deletions, one file changed.

Fixes an issue where Matrix polls would accept more than 20 options despite the Matrix MSC3381 protocol capping poll options at 20. target.title: fix(ui): pair tool calls with earlier-sorted orphan results in chat coalescing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

For native-runtime transcripts (`anthropic-messages`), Control UI tool cards render only the "Tool output" section — the "Tool input" section never appears even though the tool call's `arguments` are present in the stored transcript. Users cannot see what inputs a tool was called with.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native runtime persists the tool call and its result as separate messages: the assistant message carries the `type:"toolCall"` block (with `arguments`), and a standalone `role:"toolResult"` message carries the output, linked by `toolCallId`.

Root cause chain (reproduced in a failing test before the fix):

1. `buildChatItems` orders items by timestamp (`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.ts`, timestamp comparator). In these transcripts the persisted result's timestamp can precede the assistant call message's timestamp, so the result sorts before its call.
2. `coalesceToolActivityMessages` scans forward only: a result seen before any registered call becomes an orphan (pushed unmatched), and when the call message arrives later nothing looks back at the orphan — `mergeToolCallResultPair` never runs for the pair.
3. The card is then built from the result message alone, so `inputText` is empty and the "Tool input" section is skipped — exactly the two-array pairing failure described in the issue.

The fix mirrors the existing forward pairing: remember orphaned results by call id (`openResultIndexes`), and when an assistant message with that single unresolved call id arrives later, merge backward into the result's timeline slot. The same non-tool boundary that closes the call window also clears the result window, and the existing single-call takeover branch is untouched.

## Changes

- **`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.ts`** — track orphaned tool results by call id in `coalesceToolActivityMessages`; when the call message arrives after its earlier-sorted result, merge backward into the result's slot (reuses `mergeToolCallResultPair` and `refreshOpenCallIds`; boundary clearing now resets both windows)
- **`ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.native-tool-input.test.ts`** — new coverage for the native transcript shape: call+result as separate messages (in order, via toolMessages, listed out of order, and with the result timestamp preceding the call — the failing case before this fix)

## Evidence

### Test command

```
npx vitest run ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.native-tool-input.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.question.test.ts
```

### Test output

Before (reproduction on unmodified main — the earlier-timestamp case fails, two half cards instead of one merged card):

```
x renders both input and output when the result timestamp precedes the call
AssertionError: expected [ { ...(7) }, { ...(6) } ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
```

After (this change):

```
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  127 passed (127)
```

(4 new native-shape tests, plus the full chat-thread and chat-thread.question regression suites.)

### Behavior

- Before: opening a native-runtime session in the Control UI shows tool cards with only "Tool output"; the stored `arguments` are never rendered
- After: the card merges both sides and shows "Tool input" and "Tool output"; transcripts where the call sorts before the result (the already-working shapes) are covered by regression tests and unchanged

## Related

Closes #110769
For contrast, #81099 shows tool input rendering working for the claude-cli transcript shape — this fix addresses the anthropic-messages shape specifically.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

Implemented with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed and understand every changed line; the evidence above is real local terminal output (Node 24.15.0, Windows).

## Summary
Add `.catch(() => undefined)` to `void response.body?.cancel()` in redirect handling.

## What Problem This Solves
`void response.body?.cancel()` in the redirect path discards the return value but NOT Promise rejections. If the stream is already errored, `cancel()` rejects as unhandled.

**Code evidence**: [fetch-guard.ts:701](src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts#L701)

## Evidence
- **Before**: `void response.body?.cancel()` — unhandled rejection on errored stream
- **After**: `void response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` — safe

## Real Behavior Proof

```diff
-        void response.body?.cancel();
+        void response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
```

Matches established codebase pattern (15+ existing instances).

target.title: feat: bind signed ClawHub default feed trust
target.body:
## Summary
- bind each configured marketplace profile to an expected feed payload identity; signed profiles require `feedId`
- preserve bundled/environment trust when `clawhub-public` is customized, while allowing only an explicit `verification` override to downgrade or replace it
- prepare the built-in profile for ClawHub's production Ed25519 trust root and bind it to `clawhub-official`
- support paired key-id/public-key environment overrides, failing closed before fetch when incomplete unless the profile explicitly supplies verification
- require signed feeds to carry valid `expiresAt > generatedAt`; reject expired fresh authority
- preserve expired and legacy no-expiry snapshot visibility across 304, offline, and error fallback while removing feed and manifest install authority
- retain legacy signed snapshot sequence state for rollback comparison so upgrades do not deadlock
- document trusted public-key distribution without bootstrapping from a feed-host key endpoint

## Dependencies
- ClawHub stored-catalog signer: https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3005
- signed snapshot key-rotation fix: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108342
- corrected hosted-feed v1 specs: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/39

## Deployment dependency
This PR intentionally does not invent a production key. Before making the default profile signed in production, ClawHub must generate the Ed25519 keypair, retain the private key in its deployment secret storage, and hand the matching public key and key ID to OpenClaw. That public trust root belongs in `DEFAULT_OFFICIAL_EXTERNAL_PLUGIN_CATALOG_CLAWHUB_TRUSTED_KEYS`; the private key must never enter this repository.

## Validation
- focused default trust/expiry/migration proof: 9 passed
- complete non-SQLite catalog suite: 41 passed, 2 skipped
- the two SQLite cases are locally blocked because Node 24.14.0 embeds SQLite 3.51.2 and OpenClaw requires the WAL-safe Node 24.15.0+ runtime
- scoped `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `git diff --check`
- final `codex review --uncommitted`: no discrete actionable correctness issues

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
A customized built-in profile could silently lose default trust, signed feed authority was not bounded by payload expiry, and a legacy signed snapshot without expiry could block acceptance of a newer valid feed.

Real environment tested:
Windows PowerShell at exact head `fe939bc302aec3ec1bd384145a024fb24dfe932d`, source harness with generated Ed25519 keys, mocked HTTP responses, and in-memory persisted snapshots. No live ClawHub production signing key exists yet.

Exact proof covered:
1. Configured `clawhub-public` inherits paired environment trust; an explicit unsigned profile remains authoritative even with an incomplete env pair.
2. Matching signed payloads are accepted and cross-feed replay remains rejected.
3. `expiresAt` must parse, follow `generatedAt`, and remain in the future for fresh authority.
4. Expired 304, offline, and HTTP-error snapshots remain visible with `state: unavailable` and no feed or manifest install metadata.
5. Legacy signed snapshots without `expiresAt` remain non-installable but retain monotonic rollback state and do not block a newer valid signed feed.

What was not tested:
Live ClawHub signing and the bundled production public key, because ClawHub has not generated or handed off that key yet. The two SQLite tests require a newer local Node runtime.

target.title: fix(acp): /acp sessions exposes every gateway session to non-owner senders
target.body:
Closes #103055

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where any sender allowlisted via `commands.allowFrom` (but not in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` and not the owner) could run `/acp sessions` and enumerate every ACP session on the gateway: labels, active agent ids, runtime mode and state, backend, and thread bindings for sessions created by other senders and by the owner.

The docs (`docs/tools/acp-agents.md`) state that `/acp sessions` "reads the store for the current bound or requester session" and that it is safe for authorized non-owner senders. The handler never actually applied that scope: `handleAcpSessionsAction` called `listAcpSessionEntries`, which selects all rows from the shared `acp_sessions` table, and used the caller's own session key only to place a `*` marker on the matching row.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the requester-scoping option ClawSweeper recommended on the issue: `handleAcpSessionsAction` now filters the listed entries to the caller's current bound or requester session unless the sender has owner identity (external channels) or `operator.admin` scope (internal gateway clients, which `senderIsOwner` already covers). Owners keep the full gateway-wide listing, so the diagnostic value of the command is unchanged for the people the store belongs to.

The scoping lives at the command boundary, where sender identity is known, rather than in `listAcpSessionEntries`: the store-level listing is also used by internal task-registry maintenance, which legitimately needs all rows and has no requester. The filter reuses the same `storeSessionKey === currentSessionKey` predicate the handler already used for the `*` marker, so there is one definition of "the caller's session".

Sibling read-only actions were checked: `doctor` and `install` (the other actions excluded from `ACP_OWNER_REQUIRED_ACTIONS`) report backend health and install instructions only and do not enumerate sessions. Internal gateway clients with only `operator.write` were previously able to see the full list through this same path; they are now scoped like other non-owner senders, which is the fail-closed direction for the boundary this fixes.

If maintainers prefer the fail-closed owner-gate alternative from the issue discussion (make `sessions` owner-only), that is a one-line move of `sessions` into `ACP_OWNER_REQUIRED_ACTIONS` plus a docs update; this PR intentionally preserves the documented non-owner command instead.

## User Impact

Authorized non-owner senders can still run `/acp sessions`, but the reply now contains only their current bound or requester session. Sessions belonging to other senders, channels, or the owner are no longer disclosed to them. Owners and `operator.admin` gateway clients see exactly the same gateway-wide listing as before. The docs paragraph on ACP controls now states this scoping explicitly.

Release-note context: internal gateway clients with only `operator.write` no longer see all gateway ACP sessions from `/acp sessions`; they now see only the session bound to their request scope, like other non-owner senders.

## Evidence

Real before/after run, re-verified after rebase at base commit 7a35e243c4df6566d9bc715dec111d4dd0b9620c (current main at push time; the leak reproduces there unchanged). A driver seeded two real ACP sessions into a real SQLite-backed state database (fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`) through the production `upsertAcpSessionMeta` write path, one owned by the requester (`agent:codex:acp:1111...`) and one created by a different sender (`agent:claude:acp:2222...`), then invoked the real `handleAcpCommand` dispatcher with `/acp sessions` as an authorized non-owner and as the owner, on identical inputs. Nothing in the command path was mocked: the real owner gate, the real `handleAcpSessionsAction`, the real `listAcpSessionEntries` store read, and the real state database were driven; only the inbound channel transport was replaced by directly constructed command params.

Before (pristine base), the allowlisted non-owner sender received the foreign sender's session:

```
--- /acp sessions reply to allowlisted NON-OWNER sender ---
ACP sessions:
-----
  claude (persistent, idle, backend:acpx) -> agent:claude:acp:22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
* codex (persistent, idle, backend:acpx) -> agent:codex:acp:11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```

After (this patch, identical inputs), the non-owner sees only their own session and the owner still sees everything:

```
--- /acp sessions reply to allowlisted NON-OWNER sender ---
ACP sessions:
-----
* codex (persistent, idle, backend:acpx) -> agent:codex:acp:11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
--- /acp sessions reply to OWNER ---
ACP sessions:
-----
  claude (persistent, idle, backend:acpx) -> agent:claude:acp:22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222
* codex (persistent, idle, backend:acpx) -> agent:codex:acp:11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp.test.ts`: 70 passed, including the four new regression tests ("hides foreign ACP sessions from authorized non-owner senders", "lists all stored ACP sessions for the owner", "returns an empty listing to non-owner senders with no matching session", "warns when no session key resolves for /acp sessions").
- The new non-owner regression test fails on pristine base (foreign session key present in the reply) and passes with this patch.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- Not tested: a live end-to-end channel roundtrip (Telegram/Discord message transport); the command dispatch was driven at the `handleAcpCommand` entry point.

target.title: fix(codex): MEMORY.md silently truncated when memory plugin exposes only memory_recall
target.body:
Fixes #110665

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex-runtime agents backed by a `memory_recall`-only memory plugin (e.g. memory-lancedb) would have their root `MEMORY.md` silently truncated at runtime instead of being routed through the memory tool. The agent appeared to start normally but lost access to the durable memory contents that exceeded the bounded-injection budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts:48` contained only `["memory_search", "memory_get"]`. The memory-lancedb plugin registers a tool named `memory_recall` — not either of those names — so `getCodexWorkspaceMemoryToolNames` returned `[]` on such installations, `memoryToolsAvailable` was `false`, and `MEMORY.md` fell into the bounded-injection path where it could be truncated.

The fix adds `"memory_recall"` to the set (one line). `memory_recall` is a first-class recall tool: it appears in `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` and is listed as the sole tool in `LANCEDB_ACTIVE_MEMORY_TOOLS_ALLOW` (`extensions/active-memory/types.ts:31`). Its omission from `CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` was an oversight, not a design choice.

The `doctor --lint bootstrap-size` check (issue ask #2) is **not** addressed here. Making that check runtime/harness-aware requires importing Codex extension logic into core or duplicating classification there — a cross-package change that warrants its own PR. A follow-up issue is recommended if maintainers want that diagnostic accuracy improvement tracked separately.

## User Impact

Agents using memory-lancedb (or any plugin that exposes `memory_recall` instead of `memory_search`/`memory_get`) will now have their root `MEMORY.md` correctly routed through the memory tool. The file will no longer be injected as bounded context and will not be truncated. Installations that do not expose `memory_recall` are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Failing before the fix** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`):

```
FAIL extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
  Codex app-server attempt context
    × treats memory_recall as a Codex workspace memory tool
      AssertionError: expected [] to include 'memory_recall'
    × routes MEMORY.md through tools when only memory_recall is exposed
      AssertionError: expected false to be true
        → context.memoryToolRouted
  5 pre-existing tests passed
```

**Passing after the fix:**

```
PASS extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
  Codex app-server attempt context
    ✓ treats memory_recall as a Codex workspace memory tool
    ✓ routes MEMORY.md through tools when only memory_recall is exposed
    ✓ ... (5 pre-existing tests)
  7/7 pass  EXIT=0
```

## Second commit — unrelated test-fake fix to unblock CI (please read)

This PR contains a **second commit** (`test(codex): restore getInstanceId on app-server test fake clients`) that is **not part of the memory_recall fix**. I'm flagging it explicitly so it isn't mistaken for a change in behaviour.

Why it's here: commit f14947d2 (#110587, merged earlier today) added a `state.client.getInstanceId()` call in `startCodexAttemptRuntime` (`run-attempt-start.ts:166`) but did not update the app-server **test fake clients**, which don't implement `getInstanceId`. Those tests only run under the `--changed` test selector, so the breakage stayed dormant on `main` and surfaces on any PR whose changed files land in their import graph — this PR's one-line change to `attempt-context.ts` does exactly that. The result on `main` today (verified on a clean checkout, and on f14947d2's parent) is:

- `run-attempt-thread-cleanup.test.ts` and `auth-profile-runtime-contract.test.ts` fail with `TypeError: state.client.getInstanceId is not a function` (surfacing as `expected [ 'thread/start' ] to include 'turn/start'`).
- The `run-attempt.test.ts` / `run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts` shards **stall** (no output for 300s → killed, exit 143) from the same throw.

The second commit adds `getInstanceId` to the four fake-client method sets, which clears all of the above. Happy to split this into its own PR if you'd prefer — it's a standalone `main` breakage independent of the memory fix.

**One remaining local failure that is NOT introduced by this PR:** `run-attempt.turn-watches.test.ts > counts pending user input requests as turn attempt progress` fails locally (`onBlockReply` not called within the `waitFor`). I confirmed it **also fails on the parent of #110587** (before `getInstanceId` existed), so it is a pre-existing dormant-test issue unrelated to both #110587 and this PR — most likely a timing artifact of my slower local sandbox against the 5s `waitFor`. I deliberately did **not** touch it rather than paper over a possibly-real assertion. Flagging for your awareness.

Verification run locally (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run` on the affected files): the four previously-broken files pass (41/41), and the previously-stalling `run-attempt` shards complete in ~23s with 208/209 passing (the 1 failure being the pre-existing `onBlockReply` test above).

---

This fix was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code) as part of a supervised bug-fix pipeline. The root-cause analysis, diff, and test evidence were independently reviewed (adversarial pass confirmed no other reference to `CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` exists, no snapshot hardcodes the set, and `run-attempt.test.ts` fixtures are unaffected) before this PR was submitted. Please review with the same scrutiny as any external contribution — and feel free to close if this doesn't fit the project's direction.

target.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway
target.body:
## Summary

- install grouped Claw cron declarations through the gateway-owned `cron.add` API
- persist pending, complete, failed, or removed ownership references keyed by final agent id and declaration id
- expose cron ownership in status, round-trip complete declarations through export, and include exact cron state in remove consent
- disable Claw-owned recurring work before agent config, package, or workspace cleanup
- compose existing OpenClaw config, session, workspace-safety, and trash primitives without changing ordinary agent deletion behavior

## Contract

- scheduler mutation stays in the gateway; Claws never write the cron store directly
- declaration keys are scoped as `claw:<agent-id>:<manifest-job-id>`, so package-local ids do not collide globally
- response-lost retries reconcile by declaration key before issuing another `cron.add`
- `main` declarations target `session:agent:<final-agent-id>:main`; `isolated` remains isolated, and strict v1 validation rejects other session modes
- removal calls `cron.remove` before any agent/config mutation and records partial state if recurring work cannot be proven disabled
- Claw removal uses provenance-aware cleanup around shared lower-level OpenClaw primitives; the normal `agents delete` command and gateway behavior are unchanged
- the durable install record retains its last completed phase (`config_committed`) when cron installation fails, while the command result is `partial` and includes failed cron provenance for retry/doctor

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102306 grouped export
- This PR: gateway-owned cron mutation, provenance, status, export, and removal
- Next: #102406 validated MCP ownership

All behavior remains gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

## Validation

- 59 focused cron, provenance, lifecycle, and ordinary agent-delete tests passed on exact head `344d024f8b5`
- scoped Oxfmt, Oxlint, and `git diff --check`: passed
- emitted `cron.add` payload is validated by the gateway protocol validator
- fresh GitHub CI is running after correcting the stale type/test fixtures found by the preceding run

## Real behavior proof

The lifecycle tests prove consent-bound add, scheduler-id provenance, response-lost reconciliation, status/export visibility, and removal ordering. A scheduler failure returns partial with `agentRemoved: false`; successful removal disables Claw-owned recurring work before the provenance-aware local lifecycle proceeds.

target.title: fix(synology-chat): stop fabricating send message ids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Synology Chat outbound sends fabricated a platform message id. After the incoming-webhook `sendMessage`/`sendFileUrl` calls resolve with a bare `true` (`extensions/synology-chat/src/client.ts:96`, `:132` — `Promise<boolean>`, no id in the webhook contract), the adapter returned `messageId: \`sc-${Date.now()}\`` and stamped that synthetic id into the delivery receipt's `primaryPlatformMessageId`, `platformMessageIds`, and `parts` (`extensions/synology-chat/src/channel.ts`). Downstream consumers treat `messageId` as a real platform id (e.g. delivery-pin lookup in `src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`), so a fabricated id can be acted on as if it were deliverable platform state. This is the same shape as the merged nostr fix #110006, which removed the synthetic `nostr-${Date.now()}` id in favor of an honest send result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin-sdk contract already defines the sanctioned representation for "no platform id": the empty string sentinel. `createEmptyChannelResult` documents that "empty message ids are the legacy 'no platform id' sentinel expected by outbound callers" (`src/plugin-sdk/channel-send-result.ts:55`), and `buildChannelSendResult` normalizes a missing id to `""` (`src/plugin-sdk/channel-send-result.ts:120`). Sibling channels that receive no platform id from their transport (qqbot `extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts:52`, googlechat `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.adapters.ts:52`) pass an empty `results` array to `createMessageReceiptFromOutboundResults`, producing a receipt with no platform ids and no parts. This change adopts exactly that shape: `messageId: ""` and a receipt built from an empty results array (keeping `threadId` = chat id for routing context only). Note the receipt builder falls back from `messageId` to `chatId` when resolving a part id (`src/channels/message/receipt.ts:17-27`), so passing the chat id alongside an empty message id would have re-laundered the chat id into a fake platform message id; the empty-results form avoids that. Downstream is safe for the sentinel: the delivery-pin path explicitly guards `if (!params.messageId)` (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts:1075`), and result aggregation uses truthiness (`deliver.ts:2572`, `:2618`). Scope is limited to the two send paths; no SDK or core changes.

## User Impact

Successful Synology Chat text and media sends now report an empty message id and a receipt with no platform message ids instead of a plausible-looking but fake `sc-<timestamp>` id. Delivery itself is unchanged; only the reported send metadata becomes honest. Operators relying on delivery receipts will no longer see synthetic ids that cannot be resolved on the NAS.

## Evidence

- Precedent: #110006 (merged) removed the identical `nostr-${Date.now()}` fabrication in the nostr adapter.
- Tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/synology-chat` — with the fix, `channel.test.ts` is 40 passed / 41 total, and the full plugin suite shows 120 passed with 3 failures that reproduce identically on unmodified `origin/main` (`5143d909b9`): two setup-wizard prompt failures in `core.test.ts` and `setup status honors the selected named account` in `channel.test.ts` (locale-dependent wizard prompt expectations, unrelated to this change).
- Reverse verification: with only `channel.ts` stashed, the three updated/new assertions fail (`declares message adapter durable text and media with receipt proofs`, `sendText returns an honest empty-id result on success`, `sendMedia returns an honest empty-id result on success`); with the fix restored, all three pass.
- New/updated coverage: `sendText`/`sendMedia` success tests now assert `messageId === ""`, `receipt.primaryPlatformMessageId === undefined`, empty `platformMessageIds`/`parts`, and `receipt.threadId === chatId`; the message-adapter capability proof test asserts the same honest receipt shape for both text and media.
- Typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` — zero errors in touched code; only the 3 pre-existing `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` errors that also occur on clean `origin/main`.
- `git diff --check` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on both touched files.
- Diff stat: 2 files, +43/-20 (prod `channel.ts` net −6 lines).

target.title: fix(scripts): bound release CI summary GitHub lookups

## What Problem This Solves

The release CI summary helper performs multiple sequential `gh` API reads during full release validation. Each read used `execFileSync` without a timeout, so one stalled GitHub request could block the surrounding workflow job until the 120-minute budget expires.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default `gh` runner now routes through a caller-owned `execFileSync` with a 60-second timeout and `SIGKILL`, and applies the same bound to artifact zip downloads. This keeps the release-specific latency budget local, preserves the existing 64 MiB output allowance, covers all lookups (REST reads and artifact zip downloads), and continues to fail closed when a lookup cannot complete.

The runner accepts an `execFileSyncImpl` injection point and an optional `timeoutMs` parameter, allowing the exact production options and error propagation to be tested without a slow timer-based test.

## User Impact

A release CI summary lookup no longer waits indefinitely on a stalled GitHub request. Healthy validation behavior is unchanged; a lookup that exceeds one minute now fails clearly so the release can be diagnosed or retried.

target.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a local attacker with write access to the `auth.json` parent directory can redirect credential-store bootstrap writes through a symlink. `AuthStorage` is the default credential backend for agent sessions, and its bootstrap path creates `auth.json` when the file is missing. On current `main`, a planted dangling `auth.json` symlink causes bootstrap to create, truncate, and chmod the symlink target outside the auth directory.

This also closes the follow-up hardening gap ClawSweeper found in the atomic replacement wrapper: after `@openclaw/fs-safe` renames the temp file into place, it performs a best-effort final `chmod` by target path. An attacker who can write the parent directory can swap `auth.json` back to a symlink in that post-rename window and redirect the chmod to another path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is in `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts`, `FileAuthStorageBackend.ensureFileExists()`:

```ts
private ensureFileExists(): void {
  if (!existsSync(this.authPath)) {
    writeFileSync(this.authPath, "{}", "utf-8");
    chmodSync(this.authPath, 0o600);
  }
}
```

`existsSync`, `writeFileSync`, and `chmodSync` all operate on the final path. When `auth.json` is a symlink to a missing target, the check sees no existing target and the create/chmod operations land on the symlink target.

The existing persist path already uses `replaceAuthFileAtomic()`, which writes a sibling temp file with the requested file mode and renames it into place. This PR routes bootstrap through that path:

```ts
private ensureFileExists(): void {
  if (!existsSync(this.authPath)) {
    this.replaceAuthFileAtomic("{}");
  }
}
```

To close the active swap gap, `src/infra/replace-file.ts` now wraps both async and sync `replaceFileAtomic` calls so OpenClaw sets the temp file to the requested or preserved mode before rename through a no-follow file descriptor, then skips the redundant final chmod of the replacement path. The wrapper keeps parent-directory chmod behavior and exact final file modes while removing the post-rename target-path chmod that can follow a swapped symlink. If fs-safe takes its copy fallback, the wrapper restores the resolved mode on the opened destination descriptor instead of chmodding the final path. The async wrapper resolves preserveExistingMode lazily inside the serialized replacement phase, so same-path queued writes preserve the mode left by the earlier replacement instead of an old pre-queue stat.

## User Impact

Operators no longer expose an arbitrary-file create/truncate/chmod primitive through the credential store when `auth.json` is absent and its parent directory is writable by another local user. Normal behavior is unchanged: missing `auth.json` is still created as a real `{}` file at mode `0o600`.

## Evidence

Local verification:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/replace-file.test.ts src/infra/json-files.test.ts`: 2 files passed, 24 assertions passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.symlink-bootstrap.test.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.test.ts`: 2 files passed, 3 assertions passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/infra/replace-file.ts src/infra/replace-file.test.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.symlink-bootstrap.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/replace-file.ts src/infra/replace-file.test.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.symlink-bootstrap.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- Added a same-path async preserveExistingMode regression that queues a 0644 replacement ahead of a preserveExistingMode replacement and verifies the queued write keeps 0644.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `AuthStorage` bootstrap no longer writes through a planted `auth.json` symlink, and OpenClaw's atomic replacement wrapper no longer chmods a symlink target swapped into place after rename while still preserving exact requested modes on rename, copy fallback, and queued same-path replacements.
Real environment tested: the real `AuthStorage` class from `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts` and the real `replaceFileAtomicSync` and `replaceFileAtomic` wrappers from `src/infra/replace-file.ts` were driven against real on-disk temp directories on pristine `origin/main` afe00f6c7b72f4d21f5b48b42b6792507ed7cd7d and PR head 1d2a83a50ae80f2e48654b6122eada5341c402cb. The static symlink and queued same-path scenarios used normal filesystem calls. The post-rename swap and fallback scenarios used an instrumented filesystem object only to force the relevant filesystem outcome at the production helper boundary.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-bug-repros/102853/proof-driver.ts` from `/root/openclaw`, first with `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts` and `src/infra/replace-file.ts` reset to pristine `origin/main`, then with the same files restored from PR head 1d2a83a50ae80f2e48654b6122eada5341c402cb.
Evidence after fix:

Observed result after fix: the planted bootstrap target is not created or chmodded, a symlink swapped into the replacement path after rename does not receive the final chmod, requested 644 modes are preserved under umask 077 for both rename and copy fallback, and queued same-path preservation keeps the latest replacement mode.

target.title: fix(ui): workboard dropdowns could clip in short windows
target.body:
Related: #110621

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #110621's review finding, applied to the sibling surface: the workboard select dropdowns capped their listbox height with a viewport-only bound (`min(320px, calc(100vh - 48px))`, `260px` on narrow screens), overriding Web Awesome's collision-aware `--auto-size-available-height`. When the popup opens with little room on either side of the control — short windows, toolbars near the bottom edge — a long status/agent list could overflow or clip instead of shrinking and scrolling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same composition proven in #110621: keep the design cap but bound it by Web Awesome's computed available height, `min(<cap>, var(--auto-size-available-height, calc(100vh - 48px)))`, in both the desktop and narrow-viewport rules. The viewport fallback only applies if the variable is ever unset.

## User Impact

Workboard dropdowns (status, agent pickers) now always fit the space the popup actually has, scrolling internally instead of clipping in constrained layouts.

The identical composition was verified empirically on the settings language picker in #110621: in a 420px-tall viewport the listbox's resolved max-height followed `--auto-size-available-height` (216px), stayed fully on-screen, and scrolled internally. target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote-media downloads could hang indefinitely when an upstream CDN
accepted the connection, returned headers (and optionally one body chunk), then
stopped sending data. Two channel-owned callers were missing a body-idle bound:

- `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` called `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with no
  header/idle timeouts
- `file-utils.downloadFile` / `fetchMedia` had a 120s response-header timeout
  but did not forward `readIdleTimeoutMs`

## Why This Change Was Made

Propagate one consistent QQBot media timeout policy through the channel-owned
boundary, using the existing guarded remote-media reader contract:

- `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000`
- `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000`

`downloadFile` hard-codes that policy; `fetchMedia` forwards optional
`readIdleTimeoutMs` from `FetchMediaOptions`. No new downloader or config key.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled QQ media body could leave inbound/outbound media handling
waiting forever and retain Gateway resources.

**After:** Stalled bodies fail closed after 30s without data
(`Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms`), releasing the
connection. Completing transfers are unchanged. Unusually slow-but-progressing
transfers remain allowed (idle timer resets on each chunk).

target.title: fix: recover final replies after settled tool-only turns
target.body:
Closes #108738

AI-assisted: implemented and reviewed with Codex; I understand and verified the resulting runtime behavior.

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled for this repository-owned branch.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could see completed tool activity but receive no final channel reply when the model ended the post-tool assistant turn without visible text. This was reproduced across channel and model families in #108738 and can leave users unsure whether side-effecting work completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

When all tool calls have structurally settled but the current assistant turn ends empty, the shared embedded runner now performs one bounded continuation from the existing transcript to request the missing user-visible answer. The continuation exposes no tools, so completed writes cannot be repeated, and it remains excluded for active, errored, asynchronous, delivered, spawned-session, background, or intentionally silent terminal states.

This keeps the invariant in the shared agent runtime instead of adding channel- or provider-specific behavior. It also differs from the earlier approach in #93062: recovery does not replay the original prompt or require completed tools to be replay-safe; it continues from their settled results with the tool surface disabled.

## User Impact

Users receive the model's final explanation or acknowledgment after completed tool work instead of a silent turn. Existing intentional-silence and terminal delivery behavior remains unchanged, and side-effecting tools cannot run again during recovery.

## Evidence

### Live fix proof

A real Telegram adapter with a Convex-leased `telegram` credential and deterministic mock provider exercised a side-effecting write followed by an empty terminal assistant turn:

target.title: fix(process): trim UTF-8 boundary on win32 in truncated command output
target.body:
## Problem

`trimTruncatedUtf8Boundary` in `src/process/exec-output.ts` skipped UTF-8 boundary trimming entirely when `process.platform === "win32"`. On Windows, when command output exceeded `maxOutputBytes` and was truncated mid-codepoint, the partial UTF-8 bytes were left in the buffer. Downstream `Buffer.toString("utf8")` then emitted U+FFFD replacement characters in truncated command output shown to users (doctor diagnostics, cron job output, plugin command output).

## Fix

Remove the `process.platform === "win32"` bypass from the early-return guard. The trimming logic (continuation-byte trimming in tail mode, `TextDecoder({ fatal: true })` probing in head mode) is platform-independent and works correctly on win32.

## Real behavior proof

A new test `real command output with UTF-8 emoji does not produce U+FFFD when truncated` runs an actual `node -e` command that outputs 10 emoji (40 bytes) and truncates via `maxOutputBytes: 18` (4.5 emoji). The `runCommandWithTimeout` flow exercises the full capture → `finalizeCapturedOutput` → `trimTruncatedUtf8Boundary` path on real command output:

- **With fix:** Head mode keeps 4 full emoji (16 bytes), trimming the partial 5th → `stdout === "😀😀😀😀"`, no U+FFFD, `stdoutTruncatedBytes === 24`
- **Without fix (win32 bypass):** The partial code point would remain → `stdout` would contain U+FFFD

```
 ✓ |process| ../../src/process/exec.test.ts (42 tests | 1 skipped) 3237ms
     ✓ real command output with UTF-8 emoji does not produce U+FFFD when truncated
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  41 passed | 1 skipped (42)
```

The win32-specific behavior is covered by unit tests that mock `process.platform = "win32"` and verify trimming works in both head and tail modes (previously these would skip trimming entirely).

## Risk

Minimal. The fix only removes a platform bypass that prevented trimming on win32. All other platforms were already trimming correctly. The trimming logic is unchanged.

## Problem

The OpenAI TTS contract provider in `src/plugins/contracts/tts-contract-suites.ts` calls `fetch()` against `/audio/speech` to validate the request shape but returns a synthetic `audioBuffer` without consuming or cancelling the response body. ## Problem

`secondsToMs` in `src/cron/command-runner.ts` mapped every `value <= 0` (including negative misconfigurations like `-1` or `-60`) to `EFFECTIVELY_UNBOUNDED_TIMEOUT_MS` (~24.8 days). This meant a misconfigured negative `timeoutSeconds`/`noOutputTimeoutSeconds` armed a ~24.8-day deadline that could hang doctor/cron indefinitely.

## Fix (revised per review feedback)

Only treat `value < 0` (negative) as misconfiguration, returning `undefined` so callers fall back to `DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 min). **Preserve `value === 0` as the intentional "no timeout" (unbounded) value** per the existing contract in `docs/automation/cron-jobs.md`.

This addresses the P1 concern from the initial review: existing command cron jobs that intentionally store `timeoutSeconds: 0` continue to work as "no timeout" — only negative values change behavior.

- Files changed: 2
- LOC delta: +160 / -2

Two new tests run REAL commands (no `mockResolvedValue`) with a spy that observes the actual `timeoutMs` passed to `runCommandWithTimeout` while the real command executes:

| `timeoutSeconds: 0` | `ok` / `real-zero` | `2_147_483_647` (unbounded, preserved) | `2_147_483_647` (unchanged) |

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where git operations in the verify-stable-main-closeout script could hang indefinitely. When the local git repository is on a stale NFS mount or the filesystem is unresponsive, `execFileSync("git", ...)` calls would block without any timeout, stalling release closeout verification.

## Why This Change Was Made

All `execFileSync` calls to external commands must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation) and #109107 (doctor: bound legacy crontab inspection).

## User Impact

Stable-main closeout verification can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely on unresponsive filesystem operations.

- The change adds a `STABLE_CLOSEOUT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync("git", ??` call site.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/verify-stable-main-closeout.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the production `execFileSync("git", ...)` call, injected a `git` shim that blocks forever, and verified the script exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-stable-closeout-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: execFileSync("git", [...])
fixture: git waits forever
timeout: STABLE_CLOSEOUT_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
```

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur, and updates the internal callers that pattern-match those validator messages so the delimiter change does not break cross-version behavior.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/validation-errors.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

### Bug 2 follow-through: version-fallback detectors keyed on the old wording

Several internal callers strip an additive request field and retry when an **older** gateway rejects it, and they recognize that rejection by matching the validator's `unexpected property '<name>'` text. Switching the producer to `JSON.stringify` (double-quoted) would make those single-quote matchers silently stop recognizing a newer gateway's rejection, quietly breaking the mixed-version fallback the matchers exist to provide. Five such detectors match this wording: `cron-tool.ts` (`cron.list` compact), `gateway.ts` (`connect` identity-token and `node.invoke` turn-source), `sessions-resolution.ts` (`sessions.resolve` allowMissing), and `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` (`sessions.usage` timeZone).

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.
- **Detectors, all five surfaces:** add one shared `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty(message, name)` helper co-located with the producer in `validation-errors.ts` that accepts both the legacy single-quoted and the new `JSON.stringify` wording, and route every version-fallback detector through it. The mirror of `JSON.stringify` on both the producer and the matcher keeps the escaping symmetric. `context-engine/registry.ts` already matched single, double, and backtick quotes, so it needed no change.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths. All four now route through `JSON.stringify`.
- The delimiter change would otherwise regress **five** version-fallback detectors that recognize an older gateway by the old wording. All five now accept both wordings through one shared matcher, so mixed-version `cron.list`, `connect`, `node.invoke`, `sessions.resolve`, and `sessions.usage` fallbacks keep firing, and each has both-wording retry coverage.

## Verification

- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> 195 passed (engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/plugins/schema-validator.test.ts` -> 44 passed (`messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` coverage plus the JSON-token validator assertions on both validator paths).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-resolution.test.ts` -> 223 passed (each version-fallback detector parametrized over both wordings).
- `node scripts/test-projects.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.test.ts` -> 5 passed (`sessions.usage` retry parametrized over both wordings).

## Rebase note

Rebased onto current `main`, which added the changed-file TypeScript LOC ratchet (`checks-fast-loc-ratchet`): a production file already over 500 lines may not grow. The fix is unchanged in behavior but is now expressed so that no oversized file grows:

- `afterCompactionSkipFields` (new leaf module `compaction-skip.ts`) carries the engine-owned skip payload fields, so `compact.queued.ts` and `run.ts` stop duplicating the compacted and no-op branches.
- `compact.ts` hoists the shared compaction hook context once and routes the native no-op through `runSkippedCompactionHooks`, so both after-hook call sites stop repeating it.
- `messageReportsUnexpectedProperty` takes an optional request-context argument, so each version-fallback detector keeps its whole predicate in one call.
- The helper is imported from `validation-errors.js` directly rather than re-exported from the gateway-protocol index.

`node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base origin/main --head HEAD` reports no violation across the 12 changed production files.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: on a legitimate no-op compaction the engine emitted `before_compaction` with no matching `after_compaction`, so a plugin observer that pairs the two waited forever and timed out; and the schema validators wrapped property names in single quotes, so a JSON tool-calling model that copied the reported property token back emitted a malformed key and re-triggered the identical error.

Real environment tested: the real production runtime in this branch, driven through `node` (tsx ESM loader), on pristine `main`@`1708faf85b` and on PR head `27c655c778`. Bug 1 drives the real `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` entry point from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts` end to end (real session transcript on disk, real model resolution, real hook bus) with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style paired observer. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`. The detector surface drives the real `requestSessionsUsage` from `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts` against a gateway that rejects the additive `timeZone` field in each wording.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, write a heartbeat-only transcript to a real session file, and call the real `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` on it; feed a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator and parse the token a JSON model would copy back; and drive the real `requestSessionsUsage` against a gateway rejecting `timeZone` in the legacy single-quoted and the new JSON-quoted wording. The same three drivers were run first with the production files reverted to pristine `main`, on identical inputs.

target.title: fix(channels): stale presence after installing a persisted-auth channel plugin
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who dynamically install (or uninstall, enable/disable, or reload) a plugin that adds a channel with persisted auth state (for example a bundled Matrix/Signal-style channel) would keep seeing the pre-mutation channel presence list. Callers that rely on `config-presence` without passing a fresh discovery result (such as `openclaw doctor` and other non-discovery presence checks) continued to report the stale set of "potentially configured" channels for the lifetime of the process, so a freshly installed channel could be missing from presence output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache in `src/channels/config-presence.ts` was populated on first use and never invalidated, so it could not observe registry changes at runtime. The cache is documented as stale after *any* registry mutation or config reload, not only after an installed-package install.

Instead of calling the invalidation from a single install path, this wires `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` into `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` in `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts` — the single committed boundary that install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload all funnel through (via `install-persistence.ts`, `management-service.ts`, `plugins-uninstall-command.ts`, and the update paths). Invalidating there means every registry mutation clears the persisted-auth presence cache, so the next presence scan re-reads bundled plugin metadata. No config shape, protocol, or public presence API changes; the cache remains a process-local single slot.

## User Impact

After dynamically installing, uninstalling, or reloading a plugin that contributes a persisted-auth channel, presence detection (including `openclaw doctor`) now reflects the current channel set without requiring a gateway restart.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`:
  - Mocked lifecycle tests reproduce the stale-cache behavior across install, uninstall, and multi-cycle mutations, asserting the cache resets and the next read returns the updated channel list.
  - A **real (non-mocked) wiring test** imports the actual shared boundary `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` and asserts it invokes `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` — proving the invalidation is reached through the production registry-mutation path, not just a manually called helper.
- Focused suite green locally (current rebased head):

  ```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed (10)
  ```

- oxlint clean; `registry-refresh.ts` import path resolves (`../channels/config-presence.js`).

## Real behavior proof

### Environment

- pnpm v11.2.2

### Problem Statement
The module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache in `src/channels/config-presence.ts` was populated on first use and never invalidated. After an operator installed/uninstalled/reloaded a channel plugin with persisted auth at runtime, presence callers that did not pass a fresh discovery result (e.g. `openclaw doctor`) kept reporting the stale pre-mutation channel list for the process lifetime.

### Fix Summary
Added `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` function and integrated it into `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` — the shared registry-mutation boundary used by install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload operations.

target.title: fix(markdown): keep IR text slicing UTF-16 safe

## What Problem This Solves

`sliceMarkdownIR` uses `String.prototype.slice()` on code-unit positions to slice IR text. When the slice boundary falls in the middle of a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK supplementary character), the resulting text contains orphaned surrogates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce invalid Unicode strings downstream, potentially corrupting rendered markdown or downstream consumers.

## User Impact

Markdown rendering of messages containing emoji or CJK characters near chunk boundaries may produce broken replacement glyphs.

## Evidence

All 34 existing tests pass plus the new surrogate pair safety test.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: improve(gateway): bound visible history page reads
target.body:
Parent stack: #110374 must land first. This draft is based directly on `josh/clawdbot-d02.1.9.1.40-db6-generation-cursors` and contains only the visible HTTP/SSE history follow-up.

## What Problem This Solves

Deep `GET /sessions/:sessionKey/history` pages and SSE history refreshes currently materialize and deserialize the full transcript before returning a small visible page. A 50-message request against a 100,000-event active transcript therefore incurs latency and memory proportional to total transcript size.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visible JSON and SSE reads now share one internal cursor/read owner backed by the existing `session_transcript_active_events` projection and indexed keyset access from #108851. The opaque cursor is session-scoped, generation-aware, direction-aware, and anchored to a stable active event; raw delta cursors remain separate. The change does not add a projection, offset scan, schema version, or alter `chat.history`.

The shipped numeric HTTP cursor remains accepted for one upgrade window. Unsupported fallback reads preserve the caller's cursor instead of silently restarting the page.

## User Impact

Operators with deep session histories receive small HTTP history pages and SSE refreshes with bounded work. New appends do not invalidate paging toward older messages, while branch replacement or generation changes reset the visible snapshot instead of continuing from a stale anchor.

## Evidence

### Correctness and validation

- Focused accessor, state, query-plan, HTTP JSON, and SSE tests passed on Blacksmith Testbox (39 focused assertions total across the exercised files).
- Path-scoped `pnpm check:changed` passed formatting, boundary/API guards, core and test typechecks, lint, database-first guards, and import-cycle checks.

### Apples-to-apples benchmark

target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #93069.

This keeps the config contract honest without stranding existing configs:

- `diagnostics.otel.protocol` now documents and validates the only implemented transport: `http/protobuf`.
- Existing shipped configs with `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` are now handled by `openclaw doctor --fix` instead of simply becoming invalid on upgrade.
- If the old config also had telemetry enabled, doctor disables `diagnostics.otel.enabled` while removing `protocol`, preserving the old runtime behavior where `grpc` never exported telemetry.
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` remains a fail-closed runtime override path, and now has focused regression coverage.
- Real gRPC exporter support is intentionally out of scope here.

## Linked context

Closes #93069.

Related review concern: ClawSweeper flagged the first version because it rejected a shipped config value without an upgrade path. This revision adds that doctor migration path and proof.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs no longer get stranded by the stricter schema; doctor removes the unsupported protocol and disables enabled telemetry until the operator chooses an OTLP/HTTP collector.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, Node v25.6.1, branch head `074f6a0b45`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '
  const { validateConfigObjectRaw } = await import("./src/config/validation.ts");
```

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): prevent distinct titles from silently overwriting each other
target.body:
## Summary

Two distinct memory-wiki pages whose titles slugify to the same value silently overwrite each other, and the first page is permanently lost.

The agent-facing path is `wiki_apply` with op `create_synthesis`. When an agent saves a synthesis titled "Q3 Report" and later saves a different synthesis titled "Q3-Report", both resolve to `syntheses/q3-report.md` under id `synthesis.q3-report`. The second write overwrites the first: the first synthesis's managed Summary, sourceIds, claims, and confidence are gone, and neither `wiki_get` nor `wiki_search` can recover them. No error or warning is surfaced.

`slugifyWikiSegment` collapses case, spaces, and punctuation, so realistic agent-generated titles collide: "Q3 Report" / "Q3-Report", "Project Alpha!" / "Project Alpha", "Sales (2026)" / "Sales 2026", "Meeting Notes" / "meeting notes". The sibling CLI path `wiki ingest` has the same defect for `sources/<slug>.md`.

## Root cause

`extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts` derived the synthesis page path and id from the bare slug, with no disambiguation when an existing page at that slug belongs to a different title:

```ts
// before
const slug = slugifyWikiSegment(params.mutation.title);
const pagePath = path.join("syntheses", `${slug}.md`).replace(/\\/g, "/");
const root = await fsRoot(params.config.vault.path);
const existing = await root.readText(pagePath).catch(() => "");
```

`slugifyWikiSegment` only appends a hash when the slug exceeds the byte cap (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts`), so short colliding titles get no hash. `ingest.ts` had the identical pattern for `source.<slug>`.

## Fix

Add one shared identity helper and route both writers through it. The plain readable slug is reused when it is free or already owns the same title (so re-applying a synthesis still updates in place); a distinct title that lands on an existing page gets a stable title-hash suffix, matching the existing `okf.ts` hashed-identity pattern:

```ts
// after (markdown.ts)
export async function resolveTitleKeyedWikiSlug(params: {
  title: string;
  readExistingTitleBySlug: (slug: string) => Promise<string | undefined>;
}): Promise<string> {
  const baseSlug = slugifyWikiSegment(params.title);
  const existingTitle = await params.readExistingTitleBySlug(baseSlug);
  if (existingTitle === undefined || existingTitle.trim() === params.title.trim()) {
    return baseSlug;
  }
  const suffix = createHash("sha1").update(params.title).digest("hex").slice(0, WIKI_SEGMENT_HASH_BYTES);
  return `${baseSlug}-${suffix}`;
}
```

`apply.ts` (`create_synthesis`) and `ingest.ts` (`wiki ingest`) both resolve their slug through this helper before reading/writing the page.

The "existing title" is read the same way query and compile resolve a page's effective title (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts`): frontmatter `title`, then the first `# ` H1 heading, then the file name. So a page that occupies the target slug but has no frontmatter (a supported hand-authored raw source page) is recognized as occupied and gets a distinct slug for the incoming title instead of being silently overwritten. The helper also canonicalizes the title once (trimmed) and uses that single value for the base slug, the existing-title comparison, and the hash suffix, so two writes of the same logical title that differ only by surrounding whitespace land on the same page instead of forking a duplicate.

## Why this is the right boundary

- The helper lives next to `slugifyWikiSegment` and reuses the same `WIKI_SEGMENT_HASH_BYTES` and SHA-1 pattern already used by `okf.ts`/`createWikiPageFilename`. Two call sites share it (synthesis and source), so it pays rent.
- Backward compatible with no vault migration: the common single-page-per-title case keeps its plain `<slug>.md` path because the stored title matches. Only genuine distinct-title collisions get a hashed path, so existing vaults and same-title re-applies are unchanged.
- Covers both managed and unmanaged pages: collision detection compares the incoming title against the existing page's effective title (frontmatter title, else H1, else file name), so a no-frontmatter raw source page is protected, not just generated pages that carry a `title` field.
- Prior art: closed PR #65992 proposed a source-path-keyed fix for the ingest half only and was closed unmerged; merged PR #64742 fixed only the Unicode/empty-slug case. Neither touched `create_synthesis`, and the distinct-title slug collision is still live on current `main` (proof below). This change fixes the agent-facing synthesis path that no prior PR addressed, and removes the same live collision from the source path with one helper.

## Verification

From a worktree with deps (node at /opt/node/bin):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/slug-collision.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts` -> 72 passed
- `slug-collision.test.ts` regressions fail on pristine `main` and pass with this patch: distinct synthesis titles, distinct ingest titles, a no-frontmatter raw source page colliding with a generated ingest title, and a colliding title re-applied with surrounding whitespace updating its existing hashed page instead of duplicating it.
- `wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts` regressions fail on previous PR head 499bffe00e and pass with this patch: transient title-read failures during colliding synthesis creation and source ingest still allocate the distinct hash-suffixed page instead of reusing the occupied bare slug.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/slug-collision.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts` -> clean
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/memory-wiki/src/apply.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/slug-collision.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/wiki-notes-read-retry.test.ts` -> clean
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/memory-wiki/tsconfig.json` -> exit 0
- Branch rebased onto current `origin/main` 76ccd17ac3.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: distinct memory-wiki syntheses and ingested sources whose titles slugify to the same value no longer overwrite each other and silently lose the first page.
Real environment tested: drove the real `applyMemoryWikiMutation` (`create_synthesis`) and the real `ingestMemoryWikiSource` (`wiki ingest`) against temp vaults read from disk after each run, on pristine main at origin/main 9ff7abc8989c1770856b27d5b06e6bb6695ce666 with the original production files restored, on previous PR head 499bffe00e with the retry repair absent, and on PR head f7ca15a483 with this patch applied, identical inputs for each before/after pair. The transient-read run injected one filesystem `ENOENT` at the existing source page read boundary; all vault writes, page parsing, slug resolution, and disk reads stayed production code.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: apply `create_synthesis` "Q3 Report" (body "Revenue grew 12 percent", source.finance, claim.q3.revenue), then apply `create_synthesis` "Q3-Report" (body "Headcount fell 4 percent"); separately `wiki ingest` "Q3 Report" then "Q3-Report"; ingest "Q3 Report" onto a pre-seeded hand-authored no-frontmatter sources/q3-report.md; re-apply "  Q3-Report  "; then run `wiki ingest` "Q3 Report" followed by `wiki ingest` "Q3-Report" while the first read of the occupied `sources/q3-report.md` returns `ENOENT`; list each directory and read each page from disk.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main, three prod files reverted, driver identical)

  first  pagePath=syntheses/q3-report.md
  second pagePath=syntheses/q3-report.md

  first synthesis body keeps 'Revenue grew 12 percent': false
  first synthesis body keeps source 'source.finance': false

  first  pagePath=syntheses/q3-report.md
  second pagePath=syntheses/q3-report-97358135a013.md

  first synthesis body keeps 'Revenue grew 12 percent': true
  first synthesis body keeps source 'source.finance': true

  source page files (count=2): ["q3-report-97358135a013.md","q3-report.md"]
  ingest A page keeps 'finance source body': true
  ingest B page keeps 'headcount source body': true
ingest onto hand-authored no-frontmatter sources/q3-report.md
  ingest wrote to: sources/q3-report-4d84a9cac68c.md
  hand-authored q3-report.md keeps 'Hand authored raw source.': true
re-apply '  Q3-Report  ' (whitespace variant of existing 'Q3-Report')
  re-apply wrote to: syntheses/q3-report-97358135a013.md
  updates the existing hashed page in place, no duplicate: true
  synthesis page files (count): ["q3-report-97358135a013.md","q3-report.md"]

injected transient read failure: true
source page files (count=1): ["q3-report.md"]
first page keeps finance source body: false
```

Observed result after fix: on pristine main both distinct titles collapse onto one bare-slug page, the first synthesis body and source.finance are gone, neither wiki_search nor the on-disk page can recover them, and a real ingest overwrites a hand-authored raw page; on the previous PR head a transient existing-page title read still makes the colliding source write back to the occupied bare slug and lose the first body; after the patch the second distinct title gets a stable title-hash slug, both pages persist with their own body and sources even after the transient read failure, search recovers the first synthesis, the hand-authored raw page is left intact, and re-applying the same title with only surrounding whitespace updates the existing hashed page in place instead of forking a duplicate.

target.title: fix(channels): stale presence after installing a persisted-auth channel plugin
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who dynamically install (or uninstall, enable/disable, or reload) a plugin that adds a channel with persisted auth state (for example a bundled Matrix/Signal-style channel) would keep seeing the pre-mutation channel presence list. Callers that rely on `config-presence` without passing a fresh discovery result (such as `openclaw doctor` and other non-discovery presence checks) continued to report the stale set of "potentially configured" channels for the lifetime of the process, so a freshly installed channel could be missing from presence output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache in `src/channels/config-presence.ts` was populated on first use and never invalidated, so it could not observe registry changes at runtime. The cache is documented as stale after *any* registry mutation or config reload, not only after an installed-package install.

Instead of calling the invalidation from a single install path, this wires `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` into `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` in `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts` — the single committed boundary that install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload all funnel through (via `install-persistence.ts`, `management-service.ts`, `plugins-uninstall-command.ts`, and the update paths). Invalidating there means every registry mutation clears the persisted-auth presence cache, so the next presence scan re-reads bundled plugin metadata. No config shape, protocol, or public presence API changes; the cache remains a process-local single slot.

## User Impact

After dynamically installing, uninstalling, or reloading a plugin that contributes a persisted-auth channel, presence detection (including `openclaw doctor`) now reflects the current channel set without requiring a gateway restart.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`:
  - Mocked lifecycle tests reproduce the stale-cache behavior across install, uninstall, and multi-cycle mutations, asserting the cache resets and the next read returns the updated channel list.
  - A **real (non-mocked) wiring test** imports the actual shared boundary `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` and asserts it invokes `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` — proving the invalidation is reached through the production registry-mutation path, not just a manually called helper.
- Focused suite green locally (current rebased head):

  ```
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
  ```

- oxlint clean; `registry-refresh.ts` import path resolves (`../channels/config-presence.js`).

## Real behavior proof

### Environment
